entities.summary:
Konstantinos Aspietes was a Byzantine general active in the late 12th century who played a key role in the Third Crusade.

Aspietes was born in unknown circumstances and died in 1300, leaving behind a legacy of military campaigns and strategic alliances in the Holy Land.

His actions had a significant impact on the regional dynamics of the crusades, influencing the policies of the Byzantine Empire and the rise of the Mamluk Sultanate.

The memory of Aspietes has faded into history, leaving behind a complex web of historical significance and cultural heritage.
